codeql_environment.api_surface_note: Extraction queries use only `import python` AST APIs verified against the locally cached python-all 7.1.2 library: AstNode.getLocation()/getScope()/toString(), Location.getFile()/getStartLine(), File.getRelativePath(), Call.getFunc()/getArg(int), Attribute.getName()/getObject(), Name.getId(), Subscript.getObject()/getIndex(), StringLiteral.getText(), Function.getName()/getArg(int), Parameter (Name-or-Tuple node; names read via asName().getId()), AssignStmt with getATarget()/getValue() and Scope.getName() for class-scope field definitions. No AstNode.getFile(), no API::Node vs DataFlow::Node mixing, no QL classes are defined in the extraction queries, no @kind is declared (plain multi-column select for `codeql query run` + `bqrs decode`). The QL variable for module paths is named moduleHint ('module' is a QL keyword). Compile-checked pitfall (verified with `codeql query compile --check-only`, CLI 2.25.1): an inline if-then-else value is NOT accepted on the right-hand side of `=` ('expected a term but found an expression'), and a helper predicate must bind every argument in each of its disjuncts; receiver hints are therefore bound via the disjunctive predicate requestReceiverHint(Attribute, string) instead. Both extraction queries pass `codeql query compile --check-only` cleanly.

Unlike the framework-only django database of a prior run, this database contains the FULL GeoNode application: views, forms, DRF/tastypie APIs, celery tasks and models are all in scope, so source extraction anchors on the application's own request boundaries (Django request fields, DRF request.data/query_params, form fields, CLI options) instead of framework internals.

Auth/reachability facts verified in source: geonode/proxy/views.py:69-70 the /proxy/ view carries ONLY @requires_csrf_token - no login_required, no permission decorator; its host allow-list (PROXY_ALLOWED_HOSTS, checked at :140 only when not settings.DEBUG, :109) is auto-extended with every registered remote Service base_url host (:136-138). geonode/services registration requires login (views.py:57 register_service @login_required). DRF harvester writes require admin (IsAdminOrListOnly, harvesting/api/views.py:38-57) but harvester LIST is public. tastypie/DRF v2 APIs carry per-viewset permissions.

coverage_gaps: httpx / aiohttp / grequests / httplib2 are NOT imported anywhere in the geonode package - no candidate families are emitted for them, and none should be fabricated. urllib.request.urlopen/urlretrieve appear only in repo-root pavement.py (build tooling outside the geonode/ package scope) and in tests - both excluded and documented

The actual byte-level network I/O for OWSLib (WebMapService/WebCoverageService/WebFeatureService/openURL/http_post), arcrest and smart_open happens INSIDE those third-party libraries, whose source is not part of this database. Their constructor/wrapper call sites in geonode code are extracted as wrapper sink candidates; taint flow modeling into the library internals would need additional summary steps in Phase 2 (MySummaries.qll)

DRF/tastypie implicit deserialization: request.data -> serializer -> model field (e.g. HarvesterSerializer carrying remote_url) is framework glue; the extraction captures the request.data reads and the model field definitions, but the serializer-level plumbing itself may need summary edges in Phase 2

Second-order (DB-content) propagation is captured as model-field source candidates (Service.base_url, Harvester.remote_url, ResourceBase.thumbnail_url, Link.url, Document.doc_url, Dataset.ows_url, MapLayer.ows_url, monitoring Service.url); whether a given instance is attacker-influenced is a labeling/context question, not provable from the AST alone

geoserver_proxy (/gs/) builds its URL from the request path but constrains the base to ogc_server_settings.LOCATION; the extraction records its route-derived parameters as source candidates - path-prefix confinement is a labeling-stage judgment

pycsw harvest capability (csw_global_dispatch forwarding the raw QUERY_STRING to pycsw server.Csw) performs any remote fetch inside the pycsw library, which is not part of this database; only the request-entry surfaces are extracted here
